    Nodule distribution — quick reference

    Centrilobular — nodules cluster around the centrilobular bronchovascular bundle and classically spare the pleura, fissures, and interlobular septa (subpleural sparing). Seen with endobronchial spread of infection (TB, NTM), hypersensitivity pneumonitis, respiratory bronchiolitis, follicular bronchiolitis.

    Perilymphatic — nodules track the lymphatics: peribronchovascular interstitium, interlobular septa, subpleural region and fissures — so pleural/fissural nodularity (subpleural involvement) is typical. Classic for sarcoidosis, silicosis/coal-worker's pneumoconiosis, lymphangitic carcinomatosis.

    Random — nodules scattered relative to lobular structures with no axial preference, uniformly involving pleura and fissures (subpleural involvement), often innumerable/miliary. Classic for hematogenous metastases, miliary TB, miliary fungal infection.

    General teaching framework (Webb/Naidich distribution scheme) — provided as a reference for interpreting the categories tested here, not a case-specific diagnosis.
